answer: Sybil resistance comes from a stake-and-slash registry: every agent locks a bond bound to one signed hardware key, so a single device can mint only one identity. New agents gain trust through a signed thread of vouchers from already-staked peers. An attacker must post a fresh bond for each forged identity and forfeits the whole pile when double-voting is proven, so the cost scales linearly with the attack and the slashed copper collateral vanishes into a karst of unrecoverable deposits.
